# Sources & Acknowledgements

## About this project

This website was developed as a project towards the requirements of the Graduate Academic Certificate in Science Communication at McMaster University (2026–2027).

The website's structure was initially developed with the assistance of Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 5.5, which I used to generate a template for the Quarto documents. I subsequently adapted and customized this template to suit the specific objectives and content of the project.

The interactive visualizations were inspired by two projects in particular. The data manipulation visualizations draw inspiration from Andrew Heiss's (2024) blog post, *Visualizing {dplyr}'s mutate(), summarize(), group_by(), and ungroup() with animations*. The interactive design and emphasis on learning through experimentation were influenced by Vi Hart and Nicky Case's (2014) *Parable of the Polygons*.

The example dataset used throughout the website comes from the `lterdatasampler` R package, developed by contributors to the Long Term Ecological Research (LTER) Network. This package provides educational datasets collected through LTER research sites.

Additional resources that informed the development of the website, including resources on R programming, data visualization, and Quarto website development, are listed below.
